summary: Marie-Stella Boussemart studied under Samten Gyaltsen Karmay and Dagpo Rinpoche.

Marie-Thérèse de Mallmann was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology scholar. She studied at the École du Louvre, EPHE, Institut d'art et d'archéologie, and Collège de France, later working at the CNRS (1942–1974) and Guimet Museum (1948–1975).

Marielle Harrison works in religious and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Washington and University of Chicago, later serving as a teaching fellow at Chicago (2025–2026) and a postdoctoral fellow lecturer at Stanford (2026).

Mariia Lepneva specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She studied at MGIMO and Buryat State University, taught Chinese at MGIMO and HSE, and became a postdoctoral researcher at Ghent University (2023–2026).

Marijan Molé was a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and religious studies. He studied at Ljubljana, Jagiellonian University, EPHE, and Paris, holding posts at Jagiellonian (1947–1950), the CNRS (1950–1955), and IFRI (1955–1959).

Marilyn Hirsh was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology scholar who studied at Carnegie Mellon University (ca. 1961–1965). She taught Indian and Buddhist art at Cooper Union and the Institute of Fine Arts, New York University.

Marina Illich specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Columbia University by 2006, studying under Robert A. F. Thurman, Ryuichi Abe, Angela Zito, and John Stratton Hawley.

Marina Rimscha is an Indologist and linguist who earned her MA and Dr. Phil. at the University of Bonn. She held teaching and research posts at Bonn, Hebrew University, Haifa, and Technion (2025–2026).

Mario Bonardi worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied under Carlo Formichi and Giuseppe Tucci, later holding posts at the Italian Institute for Africa and the East and Sapienza University of Rome.

Mario Bussagli was an archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian, and Indology scholar. He earned his doctorate under Giuseppe Tucci at Sapienza University of Rome, where he served as docent from 1957 to 1987.

Mario Cappieri was a scholar of Indology and archaeology. He served as a lecturer in demography at Sapienza University of Rome and as a professor of anthropology at the University of Naples Federico II in 1955.
Mario D'Amato is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under Paul J. Griffiths and held positions at Hampshire College and Rollins College.

Mario Daza de Campos was an Indology scholar who studied under Francisco García Ayuso. He served as ordinary professor of Sanskrit at Complutense University of Madrid, succeeding Enrique Soms y Castelín in 1897.

Mario Poceski specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr. and joined the University of Florida in 2001 after teaching at the University of Iowa.
Mario Praz studied at the Universities of Bologna and Florence. He held academic posts at the University of Manchester (ca. 1932–1934) and Sapienza University of Rome (ca. 1934–1966).

Mario Vallauri was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Naples, Florence, and Würzburg under Kerbaker, Pavolini, and Jolly. In 1922 he became libero docente of Sanskrit at the University of Turin, lecturing there from 1924 to 1931.

Marion L. Matics specialized in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology, earning a PhD at Columbia University in 1960 under Horace L. Friess. Matics taught Oriental philosophy at Columbia University and Brooklyn College.

Marion Meyer is an archaeology scholar who studied at Bonn and Munich. She held academic posts at Munich, Hamburg, and Bonn, and served as full professor at the University of Vienna from 2003 to 2020.

Marion Rastelli is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned her doctorate under Gerhard Oberhammer. She has held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (attested 2019) and the University of Vienna as a lecturer (attested 2020–2026).
Marius Zemp is a linguistics and Tibetology scholar. He earned his Lizentiat at the University of Bern (1999–2014) and served there as a lecturer from 2020 to 2025.
